content: Transient erythroblastopenia of childhood (TEC) is a form of anemia that develops gradually during early childhood. It is primarily characterized by the slow onset of pallor, which is a noticeable paleness of the skin. The exact cause of TEC remains unknown. However, there is evidence suggesting that an infection with Parvovirus B19 may play a role in its development. Most children affected by TEC recover fully within a period of one to two months. The median age at which TEC typically presents is between 18 and 26 months. However, the condition can also occur in infants younger than six months and in children as old as ten years. Due to the gradual progression of anemia in TEC, affected children often appear healthier than one might expect given their significantly low hemoglobin levels.
